artists.biography:
Tears for Fears are an English rock band formed in 1981 by Roland Orzabal and Curt Smith.
Founded after the dissolution of their first band, the mod-influenced Graduate, they were initially associated with the New Wave synthesizer bands of the early 1980s but later branched out into mainstream rock and pop, which led to international chart success.
Their platinum-selling debut album, The Hurting, reached number one on the UK Album Chart, while their second album, Songs from the Big Chair, reached number one on the U.S. Billboard 200, achieving multi-platinum status in both the UK and the United States. Following the release of their third platinum-selling album, The Seeds of Love (1989), Smith and Orzabal parted company in 1991, though Orzabal retained the Tears for Fears name throughout the remainder of the 1990s. The duo re-formed in 2000, and released an album of new material, Everybody Loves a Happy Ending, in 2004. To date, Tears for Fears have sold over 25 million albums worldwide, including more than 8 million in the U.S.

perplexity.description:
Rule the World is a 2017 greatest hits compilation by Tears for Fears, released by Virgin EMI Records, spanning the band's career with 16 tracks blending electronic, rock, and pop elements. It prominently features iconic singles from their breakthrough second album Songs from the Big Chair (1985), such as "Everybody Wants to Rule the World" and "Shout," alongside hits like "Mad World" from The Hurting (1983), "Sowing the Seeds of Love" and "Advice for the Young at Heart" from The Seeds of Love (1989), and others including "Head over Heels," "I Believe," and "Mothers Talk."

The collection captures Tears for Fears' evolution from the dark, synth-driven introspection of their debut—powered by drum machines, Fairlight CMI samplers, Yamaha DX7, PPG Wave, and Sequential Prophet-8—to the glossy, anthemic production of Songs from the Big Chair, which topped the US charts and earned multi-platinum status with socially conscious lyrics and influences from Beatles-esque pop to politically charged rock. Tracks like the No. 1 US hit "Everybody Wants to Rule the World," originally titled "Everybody Wants to Go to War" and recorded in under two weeks, exemplify their shift to a bouncy 12/8 shuffle and MIDI-sequenced sophistication, while "Shout" became a global staple.

Released as a two-disc LP set, Rule the World includes two new tracks and remixes like the US Remix of "I Believe," underscoring the band's enduring legacy with Brit Awards wins, film soundtracks (e.g., Donnie Darko), and covers by artists like Lorde. Critics praise its "high-gloss" mid-80s zeitgeist and innovative techniques that positioned Tears for Fears as pop forebearers, making this a definitive overview of their chart-topping, generation-defining sound.
